question: Can a reporting-alpha allocation pair be chosen after seeing the same V3 evidence while still guaranteeing that both selected bounds cover with probability at least .95, and can a selection-rule-aware construction beat all-pairs union insurance?

same_history_counterexample.construction: Two independent valid e-values. For each channel, E=1/.045 with probability .045 and E=0 otherwise, so E[E]=1. After observing both, choose allocation (.045,.005) if channel 1 is high, otherwise choose (.005,.045) if channel 2 is high; both pairs are members of the nine-split grid.
same_history_counterexample.conclusion: The constraint alpha_equal+alpha_exposure=.05 does not by itself protect classical selected-pair SoS coverage when the split is chosen from the same evidence. The failure is exact, not Monte Carlo.

e_by_vs_strict_sos.derivation: If exactly two intervals are selected, FCR=E[V]/2. Therefore P(any selected interval misses)=P(V>=1)<=E[V]<=2*FCR. To infer strict SoS error <=delta from FCR alone requires FCR<=delta/2. Encoding nine allocation pairs as 18 candidate intervals, e-BY at q=delta/2 with |S|=2 uses per-selected-interval alpha=q*2/18=delta/18.
e_by_vs_strict_sos.conclusion: For the stronger two-bound SoS target, e-BY/FCR is not a free replacement for simultaneous insurance; under this direct encoding the sufficient conversion collapses to the same uniform union budget.

predictable_freeze_and_confirm_theorem.statement: Let tau be a stopping time. Let the chosen allocation k_hat and channel budgets (a1,a2) be F_tau-measurable with a1+a2<=delta. After tau, start fresh channel e-processes at wealth 1 whose one-step factors are conditionally e-valid given the full past, including k_hat. Then conditional Ville bounds give P(channel j ever miscovers after tau | F_tau)<=a_j. A union bound conditional on F_tau gives P(any selected bound miscovers | F_tau)<=a1+a2<=delta; averaging over F_tau yields unconditional selected-pair coverage >=1-delta. K does not appear.
requirements: Allocation is frozen before any post-selection reporting factor is observed.
Reporting evidence after tau is conditionally e-valid given all pilot information and the selected allocation.
Pilot evidence is not reused inside the fresh reporting e-process unless separately justified by a conditional/selective construction.
The two reporting channels may be dependent; the within-pair union bound does not require independence.
Optional stopping/continuation after tau remains allowed through the e-process guarantee.
predictable_freeze_and_confirm_theorem.interpretation: This is a selection-rule-aware SoS construction that removes the K-way multiplicity penalty by paying an evidence-reset/fresh-confirmation cost instead.

log_e_crossover_heuristic.rule: For a fixed selected pair k with prior mass pi_k, all-pairs insurance raises each channel log-threshold by log(1/pi_k). A fresh reset discards pilot log-evidence L_j(tau). Under a stationary log-e-growth approximation, fresh confirmation has smaller remaining log-threshold on channel j when L_j(tau)<log(1/pi_k).
log_e_crossover_heuristic.guard: This is a planning heuristic only. Choosing between insured reuse and fresh reset after inspecting the same evidence requires its own precommitted outer validity argument; do not use the inequality as an uncorrected post-hoc method switch.

synthetic_null_stress.model: Two independent fair-sign e-processes with factors 1.5 on + and .5 on -, 200000 trajectories, horizon 200, pilot 40. At the pilot, allocate .045 to the channel with the larger running-max log evidence and .005 to the other.
synthetic_null_stress.interpretation: The exact counterexample already proves invalidity. This separate stress shows the same direction in a conventional optional-stopping e-process: same-history reallocation exceeds 5%, while fresh confirmation and simultaneous nine-pair insurance stay below 5% in this tested synthetic condition.

public_evidence.title: Post-selection inference for e-value based confidence intervals
public_evidence.authors: Ziyu Xu; Ruodu Wang; Aaditya Ramdas
public_evidence.use: e-BY controls FCR for selected e-CIs under arbitrary dependence/selection and extends to stopping times; FCR is kept distinct from the stricter probability that both intervals in one selected pair cover.

public_evidence.title: Confidence Intervals for Selected Parameters
public_evidence.authors: Yoav Benjamini; Yotam Hechtlinger; Philip B. Stark
public_evidence.use: Shows that SoS intervals can exploit a known selection rule in specialized independent/top-k settings, so universal simultaneous insurance is not claimed to be universally optimal. Those assumptions do not directly match adaptive V3 same-history pair selection.

public_evidence.title: Game-theoretic statistics and safe anytime-valid inference
public_evidence.authors: Aaditya Ramdas; Peter Grünwald; Vladimir Vovk; Glenn Shafer
public_evidence.use: Supports optional stopping/continuation through e-processes and confidence sequences; the freeze-and-confirm theorem uses the standard conditional supermartingale/e-process logic after the selection stopping time.

measurement_validity_rules: Do not choose a same-history alpha split merely because its two nominal channel alphas sum to .05; this can exceed 5% selected-pair miscoverage.
FCR, SoS error, and all-candidate simultaneous coverage are different targets. For exactly two selected intervals, FCR q only implies SoS error <=2q without extra structure.

A predictable pilot-freeze-fresh-confirm architecture gives classical selected-pair SoS without a K-way grid penalty, but pilot evidence must be excluded from the fresh reporting certificate unless separately corrected.
Selection-rule-aware same-history SoS may exist under additional model/selection structure; the current result does not claim an impossibility theorem.
scope_guards: The synthetic stress is not production performance and is not needed for the exact counterexample.
The freeze-and-confirm theorem guarantees coverage for the post-selection fresh evidence process, not for an interval that silently reuses preselection V3 wealth.
The e-BY equivalence calculation is for the direct 18-interval encoding and the strict two-bound SoS target; it does not deny e-BY's FCR advantages for its intended objective.
No O, downstream, other-worker or legacy semantic state was used.
